item.title: Louise Woodward Murder Conviction Reduced to Manslaughter
item.description: British au pair Louise Woodward was convicted of second-degree murder in the 1997 death of eight-month-old Matthew Eappen. A judge reduced the verdict to involuntary manslaughter and sentenced her to 279 days already served. Massachusetts’ highest court upheld the decision.

item.title: Dawn Richard Says Diddy Threatened Her Into Silence
item.description: Dawn Richard alleges Sean Combs threatened her after she witnessed him assault Cassie Ventura. She also described abuse during their working relationship. A federal judge dismissed her lawsuit in June 2026 largely over filing deadlines rather than the truth of those allegations.

item.title: Rescuers Dug A Second Shaft To Reach Baby Jessica
item.description: In October 1987, 18-month-old Jessica McClure fell into a narrow well in Midland, Texas, becoming trapped 22 feet underground. Rescuers drilled a parallel shaft and tunneled through solid rock to reach her. After 58 hours, she was brought out alive.

item.title: The Luxury Flat Dispute At The Center Of Abby Choi’s Trial
item.description: Hong Kong model Abby Choi, 28, was killed in February 2023. Prosecutors allege a dispute over selling a luxury apartment motivated her ex-husband, his brother and their father to murder her. All three deny murder, and their trial remains ongoing.

item.title: Zheng Shuang’s Hidden Pay Led To A $46 Million Bill
item.description: Chinese actress Zheng Shuang’s 2021 surrogacy controversy was followed by a tax investigation. Authorities found she concealed income through false contracts and ordered her to pay 299 million yuan—about $46 million—in back taxes, late fees and fines. Her former partner was among those who reported her.

item.title: Sewol Passengers Were Told To Stay As The Captain Escaped
item.description: When South Korea’s Sewol ferry sank in April 2014, passengers were told to remain inside while the captain and crew escaped. The disaster killed 304 people, mostly high school students. Captain Lee Joon-seok was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Why The Cornell Seven Case Was Reopened
item.description: A former Cornell student’s lawsuit alleges seven fraternity members sexually assaulted her in October 2024. The defendants deny wrongdoing. After questions emerged about the original investigation, New York appointed a special prosecutor to review the evidence.

item.title: Beth Thomas Outgrew The “Child Of Rage” Label
item.description: Featured at six in the documentary Child of Rage, Beth Thomas described violent behavior following severe childhood abuse and neglect. Her story continued beyond those interviews: she later became a neonatal intensive care nurse and spoke publicly about her recovery.
